high_level_changes.headline: Feature Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.

high_level_changes.headline: Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

high_level_changes.headline: Dynamic Resource Allocation
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves dynamic resource allocation for ai/ml training, llm inference pods, fractional/multi-gpu workloads, and nic/fpga consumers running on nvidia/amd gpu nodes, multi-nic rdma clusters, and topology-aware hardware pools, delivering higher GPU utilization and fewer stranded accelerators via standardized device sharing and health reporting.

high_level_changes.headline: StatefulSet PVC Auto-Cleanup, Volume Health & Storage Expansion
high_level_changes.plain_summary: Improves statefulset pvc auto-cleanup, volume health & storage expansion for databases, kafka/clickhouse clusters, and stateful ai checkpoint storage running on csi storage drivers and cloud block volumes, delivering eliminates orphaned cloud disk charges when scaling down or deleting temporary StatefulSets.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.

jargon_glossary.meaning: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.

jargon_glossary.meaning: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.

jargon_glossary.meaning: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.

jargon_glossary.meaning: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers.
jargon_glossary.why_it_matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.

wheres_the_proof.text: SIG Node: SIG Node focused on stability and performance improvements in the 1.13 release.  A new alpha feature is introduced to improve the mechanism that nodes heartbeat back to the control plane.  The `NodeLease` feature results in the node using a `Lease` resource in the `kube-node-lease` namespace that is renewed periodically.  The `NodeStatus` that was used previously to heartbeat back to the control plane is only updated when it changes.  This reduces load on the control plane for large clusters. The Kubelet plugin registration mechanism, which enables automatic discovery of external plugins (including CSI and device plugins) has been promoted to stable in this release (introduced as alpha in 1.11 and promoted to beta in 1.12).

SIG Scheduling: SIG Scheduling has mostly focused on stability in 1.13 and has postponed some of the major features to the next versions. There are still two notable changes: 1. TaintBasedEviction is moved to Beta and will be enabled by default. With this feature enabled, condition taints are automatically added to the nodes and pods can add tolerations for them if needed. 2. Pod critical annotation is deprecated. Pods should use pod priority instead of the annotation. It is worth noting again that kube-scheduler will use apiVersion `kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1` instead of `componentconfig/v1alpha1` in its configuration files in 1.13.

Raw block volume support is promoted to beta, and enabled by default. This is accessible via the `volumeDevices` container field in pod specs, and the `volumeMode` field in persistent volume and persistent volume claims definitions. ([#71167](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71167), [@msau42](https://github.com/msau42))

(No, really, you MUST do this before you upgrade):   - The schema for the alpha `CSINodeInfo` CRD has been split into `spec` and `status` fields, and new fields `status.available` and `status.volumePluginMechanism` added. Clusters using the previous alpha schema must delete and recreate the CRD using the new schema. ([#70515](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70515), [@davidz627](https://github.com/davidz627))

As part of graduating the etcd encryption feature to beta, the configuration file referenced by `--encryption-provider-config` now uses `kind: EncryptionConfiguration` and `apiVersion: apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1`. Support for `kind: EncryptionConfig` and `apiVersion: v1` is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. ([#67383](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/67383), [@stlaz](https://github.com/stlaz))

SIG Cluster Lifecycle: - kubeadm has graduated `kubeadm alpha phase` commands to `kubeadm init phase`. This means that the phases of creating a control-plane node are now tightly integrated as part of the `init` command. Alpha features, not yet ready for GA are still kept under `kubeadm alpha` and we appreciate feedback on them.
Dry-run is promoted to Beta and will be enabled by default. ([#69644](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/69644), [@apelisse](https://github.com/apelisse))

SIG Auth: With this release we've made several important enhancements to core SIG Auth areas. In the authorization category, we've further reduced Kubelet privileges by [restricting node self-updates of labels to a whitelisted selection and by disallowing kubelets from deleting their Node API object](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#noderestriction). In authentication, we added alpha-level support for automounting improved service account tokens through projected volumes. We also enabled [audience validation in TokenReview](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.13/#tokenreview-v1-authentication-k8s-io) for the new tokens for improved scoping. Under audit logging, the new alpha-level "dynamic audit configuration" adds support for [dynamically registering webhooks to receive a stream of audit events](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug/debug-cluster/audit/#webhook-backend). Finally, we've enhanced secrets protection by graduating [etcd encryption](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/encrypt-data/) out of experimental.

SIG Storage: Over the last year, SIG Storage has been focused on adding support for the Container Storage Interface (CSI) to Kubernetes. The specification recently moved to 1.0, and on the heels of this achievement, Kubernetes v1.13 moves CSI support for PersistentVolumes to GA. With CSI the Kubernetes volume layer becomes truly extensible, allowing third party storage developers to write drivers making their storage systems available in Kubernetes without having to touch the core code. CSI was first introduction as alpha in Kubernetes v1.9 and moved to beta in Kubernetes v1.10. You can find a list of sample and production drivers in the [CSI Documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#csi). SIG Storage also moves support for Block Volumes to beta (introduced as alpha in v1.9) and support for Topology Aware Volume Scheduling to stable (introduced as alpha in v1.9 and promoted to beta in 1.10).

SIG Cluster Lifecycle: For 1.13 SIG Cluster Lifecycle is pleased to announce the long awaited promotion of kubeadm to stable GA, and the promotion of kubeadm’s configuration API to `v1beta1`. In this release the SIG again focused on further improving the user experience on cluster creation and also fixing a number of bugs and other assorted improvements. Some notable changes in kubeadm since Kubernetes 1.12:

SIG Cluster Lifecycle: - kubeadm’s configuration API is now `v1beta1`. The new configuration format provides improvements in - image repository management, addons configuration, and other areas. We encourage `v1alpha3` users to migrate to this configuration API using `kubeadm config migrate`, as `v1alpha3` will be removed in 1.14. The documentation for `v1beta1` can be found here: https://godoc.org/k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/apis/kubeadm/v1beta1

Use of the beta plugin registration directory `{kubelet_root_dir}/plugins/` for registration of external drivers via the kubelet plugin registration protocol is deprecated in favor of `{kubelet_root_dir}/plugins_registry/`. Support for the old directory is planned to be removed in v1.15. Device plugin and CSI storage drivers should switch to the new directory prior to v1.15. Only CSI storage drivers that support 0.x versions of the CSI API are allowed in the old directory. ([#70494](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70494) by [@RenaudWasTaken](https://github.com/RenaudWasTaken) and [#71314](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/71314) by [@saad-ali](https://github.com/saad-ali))

The alpha critical pod annotation (`scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/critical-pod`) is deprecated. Pod priority should be used instead to mark pods as critical. ([#70298](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/70298), [@bsalamat](https://github.com/bsalamat))

Kubernetes v1.13 focuses on Feature Enhancements, API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale, and Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements. For operators, this release translates 260 upstream engineering changes into lower serving costs, broader hardware/model support, and safer production rollouts.

## 1. What Are the High-Level Changes?
- **Feature Enhancements**: Improves feature enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.
- **API Server & etcd Watch/Cache Efficiency at Scale**: Improves api server & etcd watch/cache efficiency at scale for operator-heavy platforms, argo cd / flux gitops controllers, and multi-tenant clusters with 10k+ crds/pods running on control plane (`kube-apiserver`, `etcd`, `kube-controller-manager`) cpu and memory footprint, delivering cuts control-plane memory spikes by 30–50% during list storms and prevents cascading `etcd` overload outages.
- **Urgent Upgrade Notes Enhancements**: Improves urgent upgrade notes enhancements for general platform workloads and api consumers running on standard cluster nodes and runtime components, delivering operational reliability and lower maintenance toil.

## 3. What Does the Jargon Mean?
- **DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation)**: Kubernetes' next-generation API (`resource.k8s.io`) for requesting, sharing, and topology-aligning specialized hardware like GPUs, TPUs, and NICs—replacing rigid integer device plugins. Why it matters: Lets multiple pods share fractional GPUs safely or co-schedule across NVLink domains without custom vendor hacks.
- **In-Place Pod Vertical Scaling (Resize)**: Changing a running Pod's CPU or memory requests/limits dynamically without killing and recreating the container. Why it matters: Eliminates cold-start restarts and dropped connections when scaling stateful services, databases, or warm AI model servers.
- **Native Sidecar Containers (`initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`)**: First-class lifecycle support for helper containers (log shippers, service mesh proxies) so they start before the main app and terminate automatically after Batch Jobs finish. Why it matters: Fixes the classic Kubernetes bug where a finished Job hangs forever because an Istio/Envoy sidecar stays alive.
- **Linux User Namespaces (`hostUsers: false`)**: Maps the `root` user inside a container to an unprivileged non-root UID on the host node kernel. Why it matters: Dramatically reduces container-escape blast radius even for legacy workloads that require running as `root` inside the container.
- **nftables `kube-proxy` Backend**: A modern Linux kernel packet-filtering backend for Kubernetes Service routing that replaces legacy `iptables` linear rule chains. Why it matters: Cuts Service rule programming latency and CPU overhead on clusters with tens of thousands of Services.
- **CSI (Container Storage Interface)**: The standard plugin layer connecting Kubernetes PersistentVolumes to cloud block/file storage providers. Why it matters: Controls how fast stateful workloads attach disks, recover from node failures, and handle credentials.
